newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on investor Eurobond optimism.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on investor Eurobond optimism.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on investor optimism which could be linked to Eurobond issues by Russia and Moscow, dealers said on Thursday.
"Investor moods are better, given steady U.S. Treasuries along with Moscow's and (forthcoming) Eurobonds. Buying was seen both in Russia and abroad," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.

The City of Moscow launched on Tuesday a $500 million three-year Eurobond. Russia is planning a dollar-denominated Eurobond in the second half of June for at least seven years, with a roadshow due on June 11-18.
An International Moscow bank dealer said the fourth tranche, maturing in 2003, was the most actively traded, followed by the third and sixth tranches.
Dealers said the upward trend has paused, with the market apparently awaiting further sentiment from U.S. operators.
